subject: dplyr::group_by() gives error for character variable protected with I() at creation

messages.author: 9a0033d9324fcea3
messages.subject: dplyr::group_by() gives error for character variable protected with I() at creation
parts:
When I want to selectively suppress the character-to-factor conversion for a single variable in a call to data.frame(), I protect it with I().

That creates a variable with class "AsIs" but mode and typeof "character".

This seems to make it impossible to use dplyr::group_by() with the resulting data.frame.

Here's a small illustration of the problem and various workarounds I don't like, such as using stringsAsFactors = FALSE to suppress all conversion and post hoc rescue of a character variable with as.character().

https://gist.github.com/jennybc/7722cb734d9c650f9f85

I can't find evidence that anyone else has struggled with this, so maybe someone can suggest a better workflow? Or should dplyr be OK with this?

Thanks, Jenny

Thanks, David. That IS one of my workarounds in the Gist. The problem is … one of the other variables should be factors. I like expressing what I want in my first call to data.frame().

This is actually easier with read.table() and friends, due to the colClasses argument. I had sort of regarded the protection via I() as the data.frame() equivalent, granting fine control over variable class.

That is the cost of hacks -- they complicate the rest of the system....

Issue added at https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/issues/453

dplyr currently uses a whitelist approach to variable types so that we
can be sure that we are correctly computing summaries, hashes etc.

Hadley
